doc.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013

title: Welcome to Hamilton and jazz's path to art form
summary: Rowe welcomes Morgenstern; they chat about archives and how jazz moved from popular music to high art.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we are in the jazz archive at Hamilton College. It’s a privilege to have Dan Morgenstern with me today. And I just picked up a little thing from another interview you did, which puts you right with most other jazz musicians when you said, “Morning is not necessarily the best time for me.” So here we are in the morning. Anyway, welcome to Hamilton.

Thank you. It’s real pleasure to be here, and I’m so glad that I finally got to see your lair here, which is wonderful. I love all the photos. They’re different. It’s not the standard issue stuff. And it’s really fun what you’ve been doing here.

Well coming from you I appreciate that a lot. And I got to visit your lair a couple of times and I was pretty blown away by all that. It’s so interesting that the route jazz has traveled from what essentially was sort of a folk music, a popular music, to now being considered a very high art form.
